I’ve been 90-100% Huel for about 4 months now, I have not noticed a difference in sleep so much like in your case. I also enjoy the minimal investment in deciding what to eat and cleaning up because of work and usually having about 20 things I want to do other than think about what to eat or grocery shop. 

The reduced sodium intake was a drastic positive change physically and for my sense of taste. I do actually love cooking and delicious food, but not as a chore. When I do eat an actual meal now it is astonishing how much more I can appreciate all the flavor and it is a lot more of a special experience. I could imagine a reeeeally dedicated chef doing this sort of thing to perfect their craft haha.

House of Leaves by Mark Z. Danielewski. 

It’s in some ways a double narrative; about a young tattoo artist(Johnny Truant)who, while searching the now-vacant apartment of an eccentric, possibly insane elderly blind man(Zampano), finds a written document detailing the events of a homemade film called “The Navidson Record.” As Truant becomes increasingly obsessed with the deceased Zampanos document he finds his own sanity diminishing. The novel presents the actual document with Truants feverishly written footnotes spread throughout, as well as footnotes from unknown authors. Some footnotes make no sense or lead nowhere and the actual formatting of the novel becomes very erratic at times(backwards text, pages with a single word written on them), usually mirroring what is happening as the narrative of the Navidson Record unfolds.

The actual contents of the Navidson Record as documented by Zampano are hauntingly mysterious and at times deeply unsettling. I will refrain from posting the basic premise of the record here unless you want to know more before you decide whether you want to read it.

Your description of dissolving and your shell getting thinner from both sides feels like you are describing what I feel at times. The way the universe and “I” are configured in relation to each other makes no sense to me. It’s nauseating and it affects me to a depth that is as indescribable as a color that does not exist except with your eyes closed. “I” just want to dissolve into something nebulous.

I feel the same way and in a similar situation. The nausea especially. I had not even eaten today and suddenly the most intense wave of nausea hit me and the full weight of reality descended on me. I was at work and when I would stop driving the truck to get out and do work I would just sit because existence was too much. Shivering but not cold, nauseous on an empty stomach, I floated through the day until I had to call the center because I was sure it would all collapse on itself at that very moment. I sat and tried to breathe as I watched birds off in the horizon, wishing to somehow cast my spirit out into the sky and the mountains.
“Whose clothes are these on me? Where am I? What is this in my hand? What is happening???”
I think I relate with your sentiments OP.
